exposure: Gestational age at birth (23-34 weeks, 35-36 weeks, ≥37 weeks)
Infants born 35-36 and ≥37 weeks gestation by caesarean section
outcome: Receipt of single course and repeat doses of ACS
Timing of ACS administration (optimal vs suboptimal)
cohort: 47,105 live births at a tertiary level teaching hospital in Adelaide, Australia between 2006 and 2015
finding: While the use of antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) increased over the 10-year study period, less than half of administrations prior to preterm birth were optimally timed.
mod_finding: Infants born at 35-36 and ≥37 weeks gestation by caesarean section saw the greatest increase in ACS administration between 2006/7 to 2014/15.
